text: 4 Your Eyez Only Track Discussion Just curious to know if the track “4 Your Eyez Only” hit everyone else as hard as it hit me. To be 100% open, I am a white kid from the suburbs of Chicago whose life is nowhere near similar to the one depicted in this song. However, I can remember the exact time and place I was when I heard this song. The lyrics and its production just hit me so hard. To this day it makes me tear up on every single listen. The way he tells the story with such detail in the point of view of the character made me feel like I was physically there watching this person navigate life. The ending with Cole talking to this man’s daughter… just wow. It opened my eyes and educated me on how life plays out for so many people born and raised in the projects. For someone who all my life has only heard about life here from the news, movies, and rappers that either glorify it or provide vague descriptions of it, I found this track to be life-changing in the way I view growing up in the hood. I recommend EVERYONE share this song with your friends and family. And especially to older white people. This song has the power to change someone's outlook forever.

text: Born Sinner is the best J.Cole album. This is for me, the greatest album of all time. Better than any Pink Floyd, or Kendrick, or Radiohead album, and even better than other Cole records people place out to be his best. Lets paint a picture. Cole has just been signed a couple years back, to one of his idols, jay-Zs label. This in itself is huge for Cole, as he was going ballistic on his mixtapes, think tracks like Too Deep For The Intro, and the INSANE remix of Dead Presidents II. He puts out an album, Cole World: The Sideline Story, it has some really amazing songs, some less amazing songs, but most importantly, a track that goes crazy on the charts. Work Out. Cole is now a rapper on the rise, a new star, and he drops, Born Sinner, the most honest and descriptive album of all time. Anyways, Cole tells a story on this album. He starts out with Villuminati, a song that is undoubtedly quite replayable, and despite the not ill-intentioned but ignorant slur on this track, still manages a very clear opener. Cole, is not a seasoned veteran.
